Entry the first. If healing magic can mend a broken bone, why not a broken chair leg? Tested it on the third chair from the window in the east study. The leg mended better than new. The chair now refuses to wobble even when kicked, which I consider an overcorrection.

Mended forty-one panes of cracked glass in the great hall. Every one of them came back clearer than the day it was blown. Three students walked into the windows before lunch. Recording this as a success with side effects.
Restored a torn tapestry so thoroughly that the knight woven into it has started to look smug. Repair is too easy. I am bored. Next: making things that were never broken in the first place.
Created an inkwell that only refills if you say please. The staff are furious. Manners in the east wing have improved by roughly forty percent. For research purposes, of course.

Enchanted the fourth-floor staircase to tell a joke to anyone who climbs it. Most students laugh. The ones who groan are the ones who understood it. I have begun keeping a list of the groaners. They are my people.

Tuned every bell in the clock tower a quarter-tone flat to see who would notice. After eleven days, one first-year did. She was sorted into Moonveil the following term. I maintain this is a coincidence. I also maintain that it is not.

Taught a portrait in the south corridor to compliment passers-by. Within a week, three students were visiting it daily. Loneliness is a far more interesting variable than I had assumed. Must study this more gently.
Replaced the headmaster's quill with one that writes in rhyming couplets. His letters to parents have never been better received. He has asked me to stop. He has not asked me to change it back.

Arranged for every door in the castle to open one second late, for exactly one day. Observed four hundred people learn patience at once. Nobody was hurt. Several people were late. This is, I have concluded, the ideal ratio.
A pun, for the record: I told the arithmancy class that I'd been working on a theory about infinity, but I couldn't see where it was going. Nobody laughed. I laughed for an hour. Science.

Social experiment: gave two rival students a single umbrella during a storm and walked away. They arrived at supper dry, arguing, and friends. The umbrella was the control. Friendship was the result. I did not predict this and I am delighted.

Began a new notebook - not paper this time, but a gathering place where people come and go, talk, argue, make things and leave traces. A place to watch how people behave under ordinary pressure. It is the best notebook I have ever kept. It is still running.

My great work is finished. Three champions, three tasks, a maze at the end that thinks for itself. The most ambitious experiment I have ever conceived. It is perfect. It is also, I am quite certain, going to get someone killed.

Sealed the tournament plans inside the old journals, with a final page explaining why they must never be built. Some experiments are better left as thoughts. It is the only time in my life I have chosen not to find out what happens.
